story.title: Israeli Opposition Leader Condemns Attacks on Palestinian Villages as 'Jewish Terrorism'
story.summary: Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank, labeling them as 'Jewish terrorism.' The attacks involved Israeli settlers setting fire to vehicles and properties in multiple locations. In response, Israeli authorities have initiated an investigation into the incidents.

event_overview.title: About West Bank Violence
event_overview.subject: West Bank Violence
event_overview.summary: West Bank violence refers to recurring attacks, confrontations and other coercive incidents affecting Palestinians, Israeli settlers and Israeli forces across the West Bank, including damage to people, homes, farmland, livestock and essential infrastructure. The November 2026 developments concern alleged settler attacks on Palestinian communities within a wider pattern that UN humanitarian monitors document separately from other forms of violence in the territory.

facts.label: Location and context
facts.value: The West Bank, including East Jerusalem, is treated by the United Nations and the International Court of Justice as part of the Occupied Palestinian Territory; the ICJ’s July 19, 2024 advisory opinion addressed Israeli policies and practices there, including settlements and settler violence.

facts.label: Legal framework
facts.value: UN Security Council Resolution 2334, adopted in 2016, states that Israeli settlements in Palestinian territory occupied since 1967, including East Jerusalem, have no legal validity under international law. Israel disputes this characterization and maintains claims and security positions concerning the territory.

facts.label: How incidents are tracked
facts.value: OCHA has documented West Bank casualties since 2005 and settler violence since 2006, counting settler attacks that result in Palestinian casualties, property damage, or both.

facts.label: Recent pattern
facts.value: OCHA recorded more than 1,600 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties and/or property damage from January through mid-September 2026, affecting 275 Palestinian communities; reported effects included injuries, arson and damage to homes, crops, water systems and other infrastructure.

facts.label: Displacement impact
facts.value: OCHA reported that settler attacks and related access restrictions displaced more than 6,500 Palestinians between January 2023 and August 2026, alongside damage to livelihoods and essential services.

event_overview.scope_note: This Muninn timeline follows the selected November 22, 2026 attacks and related Israeli political reaction; it does not attempt to catalogue all West Bank violence, settlement activity, military operations, legal claims or wider Israeli-Palestinian conflict developments.

explore_lenses.label: Why do these arson attacks matter beyond the damage?
explore_lenses.title: Part of a wider pattern of settler violence
explore_lenses.summary: The attacks come amid a documented rise in settler-related violence and displacement across the West Bank, so their significance extends beyond the immediate property damage.

claims.text: The UN humanitarian office documented more than 1,600 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties or property damage from January through August 2026—an average of 6.7 a day, up from five a day in 2025.
Those attacks affected 275 Palestinian communities in the first eight months of 2026, nearly matching the number affected during all of 2025.
OCHA reported that settler attacks and related access restrictions were the leading recorded driver of Palestinian displacement in the West Bank in 2026 as of early September.

points: The UN humanitarian office documented more than 1,600 settler attacks causing Palestinian casualties or property damage from January through August 2026—an average of 6.7 a day, up from five a day in 2025.
Those attacks affected 275 Palestinian communities in the first eight months of 2026, nearly matching the number affected during all of 2025.
OCHA reported that settler attacks and related access restrictions were the leading recorded driver of Palestinian displacement in the West Bank in 2026 as of early September.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: OCHA’s figures describe reported incidents and humanitarian effects; they do not determine criminal responsibility for the November 22 attacks.
explore_lenses.note: Researched context; forecasts and viewpoints are labeled and attributed.

explore_lenses.label: What is the political fight over calling it terrorism?
explore_lenses.title: Competing accounts of responsibility
explore_lenses.summary: Eisenkot’s language is part of a direct dispute over whether the attacks reflect a broader failure of policy and enforcement or whether critics are prejudging an active investigation.

claims.text: Eisenkot called the overnight arson attacks “Jewish terrorism,” argued that extremist violence endangers regional stability and Israel’s security and foreign relations, and called for arrests and severe sanctions.
Eisenkot also blamed the Netanyahu government and specifically named ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich; this is his political assessment, not a finding by investigators.
Ben Gvir rejected Eisenkot’s intervention, saying Eisenkot did not know the facts or the investigation, according to The Times of Israel.

A Kafr Malik resident told AP that violence had increased after new settler outposts appeared near the village and described harassment during olive harvesting; that is a local resident account rather than an official attribution for this incident.

explore_lenses.label: What will the Israeli investigation need to establish?
explore_lenses.title: Attribution, coordination and accountability
explore_lenses.summary: Police have opened an inquiry, but the key unanswered issues are who carried out the arson and graffiti, whether the incidents were coordinated, and whether the investigation produces arrests or charges.

claims.text: Israeli police said they were investigating who set the fires and sprayed graffiti.
Israeli police also said investigations had been opened into arson, vandalism and property damage in the affected communities.
Reporting described attacks in Deir al-Sudan, Deir Abu Mash’al and Kafr Malik, including burned vehicles and homes; there were no reported injuries in the Times of Israel account.

story_report.summary: Overnight arson attacks struck several Palestinian villages in the West Bank, with reporting describing burned vehicles and homes in Deir al-Sudan, Deir Abu Mash’al and Kafr Malik. Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot denounced the incidents as “Jewish terrorism” and called for arrests and severe sanctions. Israeli police said they had opened investigations into arson, vandalism and property damage, including who set the fires and sprayed graffiti.

sections.heading: Eisenkot and Ben Gvir Clash
sections.body: Eisenkot said extremist violence endangered regional stability as well as Israel’s security and foreign relations. He also blamed the Netanyahu government, specifically naming ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich, but those remarks were his political assessment rather than an investigative finding. Ben Gvir rejected Eisenkot’s intervention, saying he did not know the facts or the investigation, according to The Times of Israel.

sections.heading: Settler Violence and Displacement Trends
sections.body: The incidents occurred against a broader rise in reported settler violence documented by the UN humanitarian office. OCHA recorded more than 1,600 attacks causing Palestinian casualties or property damage from January through August 2026, affecting 275 communities. As of early September, OCHA said settler attacks and related access restrictions were the leading recorded driver of Palestinian displacement in the West Bank that year.

unresolved.text: As of November 22, consulted reports had not identified suspects, announced arrests, disclosed forensic findings or brought charges in connection with the fires and graffiti.
The available reporting does not establish whether government policy or named ministers directed, encouraged or had advance knowledge of the specific attacks.

related_stories.title: Capture of Cartel Leader 'El Chapo Isidro' Sparks Violence in Sinaloa
related_stories.summary: Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, known as 'El Chapo Isidro' and one of the FBI's most wanted fugitives, was captured by Mexican special forces in Sinaloa during a military operation. Following his arrest, violence erupted in the region, resulting in at least 11 deaths, with reports of gunfire and chaos among civilians. The operation involved cooperation with US intelligence and included a shootout between security forces and armed members of his cartel.

related_stories.title: Fire at Indonesian Confectionery Factory Leaves Three Dead and Dozens Missing
related_stories.summary: A fire at a confectionery factory west of Jakarta, Indonesia, has resulted in at least three fatalities, with 36 individuals reported missing. The blaze, which began in a cooling unit on the third floor, has left parts of the factory severely damaged, including a collapsed roof. Firefighters continue to battle the flames more than 12 hours after the incident started, while rescue efforts are underway to locate the missing persons.
